audit.why: Even-leaning-favoured framing matches 55.08% over 768 games: immobile mage with a conditional root vs a dash assassin; his threat is scaling, not lane.

Spikes (4 entries) are the right stages: lvl 3-5 full string vs no mobility, lvl 6 cleanest kill window, 1st item all-in, late he outscales into teamfights. Shield references inside them corrected under point 4.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly cites a Ryze 'passive shield' / 'flux-shield' / 'shield regen' (whys[4], whys[5], spikes[1], spikes[2], mid, late, wants.you[1], wants.foe[2]). Riot's text for Arcane Mastery is bonus damage from mana and max-mana from AP — no shield exists. Q is mislabeled 'Flux (Q)' (it is Overload; Spell Flux is E) in early and wants.foe[0], and the root sequence is given as 'E first then Q' / 'root (E-into-Q)' when the root is W (Rune Prison) after an E Flux mark. breakdown.cooldowns had no digit.
audit.why: Kit text is authoritative: P no shield; W 11s rank 1 roots only on Flux-marked targets; Q 5s; E 3.5s; R 180/160/140s.
audit.corrected: All shield claims replaced with real facts, ability names fixed to Overload/Spell Flux/Rune Prison, root sequence corrected to E-into-W, cooldowns field now carries 11s / 5s / 3.5s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two copy-paste-bleed bullets; dosFull[2].d calls Rune Prison a 'fifteen-second invitation' when it is 11s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Bullets rewritten to match their titles; invitation now eleven seconds.

edits.before: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): matchup-defining — Point-blank root — respect the EQ chain that follows it. It governs your forward steps. - W Terrashape (element swap) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Ryze Rune Prison (Root): 11s at rank 1, 615 range — it only roots after Spell Flux marks you, so the E mark is your warning. - His Q is 5s and his E 3.5s: the poke never stops, but the root window does. - Hold your R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: With your first mythic your combo outpaces his passive shield regen; all-in through the shield rather than poking it. He has zero mobility to answer your E reset, so a caught Ryze is a dead Ryze.
edits.after: With your first item your combo outpaces his sustained mana-fed damage; all-in in one string rather than trading pokes. He has zero mobility to answer your E gap-close, so a caught Ryze is a dead Ryze.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 he pokes with Flux (Q) and can root you if he lands E first then Q, so do not path in a straight line through his spells. He has no mobility, so simply respect the root and farm with the knowledge that you win the instant your kit is complete. Take a chip trade with an auto plus Q when his Q is on cooldown. Wait for 3.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 he pokes with Overload (Q) and can root you if he lands Spell Flux (E) first then W, so do not path in a straight line through his spells. He has no mobility, so simply respect the root and farm with the knowledge that you win the instant your kit is complete. Take a chip trade with an auto plus Q when his Q is on cooldown. Wait for 3.

edits.before: From 3 onward you dominate: he cannot dash away from your E, so bait his root (E-into-Q), sidestep it, then E-Q-W onto him and stun him against terrain. At 6 your R burst blows past his shield. Keep an element ready every wave so you can commit the second he mispositions or wastes his root.
edits.after: From 3 onward you dominate: he cannot dash away from your E, so bait his root (E mark into W), sidestep it, then E-Q-W onto him and stun him against terrain. At 6 your R burst simply kills him. Keep an element ready every wave so you can commit the second he mispositions or wastes his root.

edits.before: Post-first-item your rotation kills through his shield before it can tick back up, and his lack of an escape means your E reset punishes any greed. He out-scales into late team fights, so close the game by repeatedly catching him from fog and denying his stack timers.
edits.after: Post-first-item your rotation kills him before his sustained Q-E-Q damage adds up, and his lack of an escape means your E gap-close punishes any greed. He out-scales into late team fights, so close the game by repeatedly catching him from fog and denying his stack timers.
